supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy spring ’71 set with stellar Good Lovin’ and Sugar Magnolia
ai_show_review.blurb: The performance erupts with a smoking Good Lovin' → Darkness jam, a wah‑filled Sugar Magnolia solo, and tight versions of Bertha, Truckin', and Uncle John’s Band. Jerry’s guitar glistens while Pigpen adds fiery harp on Big Boss Man; the soundboard capture is crisp despite minor clipping.
ai_show_review.review: April 13, 1971 at the Catholic Youth Center finds the Dead riding a wave of pure spring‑time electricity. The first set rolls out with punchy renditions of Casey Jones and Mama Tried before launching into a scorching Bertha that sets the tone for an evening of high‑octane playing. Highlights include a wah‑saturated Sugar Magnolia solo, a blistering Good Lovin' → Darkness jam that segues into a soulful Second That Emotion, and a tight Truckin' that launches into a powerful drum break. Pigpen’s organ may be missed in places, but his vocal fire on Good Lovin' and a scorching harp burst on Big Boss Man keep the bluesy spirit alive. The show closes with an uplifting Uncle John’s Band, leaving the crowd buzzing despite a curfew‑induced truncation. Across all four soundboard sources the recording quality is excellent—clear, crisp, and well‑balanced—making this one of the most accessible snapshots of the 1971 lineup.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crisp, clear mix; minor clipping only at song edges.

key_highlights: Smoking Good Lovin' → Darkness jam with soaring guitar and deep rhythm section interplay
Wah‑filled Sugar Magnolia solo that showcases Jerry’s scorching tone
Pigpen’s fiery harp on Big Boss Man and vocal fire throughout the set
Bill Kreutzmann’s heavy, chills‑inducing drumming on the extended drum break

band_performance.Jerry: Guitar glistens and shreds all night, highlighted by a wah‑filled Sugar Magnolia solo and soaring leads on the Good Lovin' jam.
band_performance.Phil: Bass sits in your lap with tight groove; takes lead vocal on Cumberland Blues and anchors every extended improvisation.
band_performance.Bob: Strong vocal presence on Casey Jones and other numbers, plus lively front‑stage banter that adds to the show’s momentum.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ missed at times but vocals blaze on Good Lovin' and a scorching harp solo on Big Boss Man energizes the set.
band_performance.Billy: Drums are heavy and exhilarating, especially during the drum break and the extended jam sections.
